filename: Physically Consistent Global Atmospheric Data Assimilation with Machine Learning in Latent Space.pdf
title: Physically Consistent Global Atmospheric Data Assimilation with Machine Learning in Latent Space
code_availability: Codes and model checkpoints used in this study are available at https://github.com/hangfan99/LDA_1.41.
testbed_rationale: The study focuses on developing and validating a latent-space data assimilation framework rather than curating a benchmark dataset or testbed for physics parameterizations or ML emulators.
pain_points: High dimensionality of model-space states leads to background error covariance matrices exceeding 10^12 elements, rendering direct inversion intractable without empirical approximations.

Trade-off between compression ratio and autoencoder reconstruction fidelity; excessive compression increases representation error while insufficient compression retains off-diagonal covariance correlations.
Patch-like analysis increment artifacts emerge when latent channel dimension exceeds model-space channels due to the Vision Transformer patch embedding.

L4DVar relies on end-to-end differentiable forecasting models, currently limiting its application to ML-based weather prediction systems rather than traditional CPU-based dynamical models without adjoints.
extraction_notes: The paper develops Latent Data Assimilation (LDA) using an autoencoder with Swin Transformer blocks and a FengWu-style ML forecast model. Evaluated using idealized OSSEs and real GDAS observation experiments.
